From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>

Date: 2027-05-05T09:52:00-07:00
Subject: RE: High 5xx/429s from inference endpoint - urgent

Quick triage notes (SRE):
- We've confirmed an autoscaler failure on the customer's Dedicated pool. The scaler attempted to spin up additional GPU workers but hit a quota/placement constraint in the customer region; allocator returned ENOSPC for two allocation attempts. Meanwhile the customer traffic created many inflight requests and repeated client retries, which amplified queue length and triggered 429 queue-overflow responses.
- Key indicators: sustained queue depth + high KV cache misses when new shards came online (logs attached: autoscaler-error.log).

Immediate mitigations we can enact now (need approval to change customer pool settings):
1) Allow temporary burst capacity: add +4 GPUs to the Dedicated pool for 60 minutes (requires manual capacity assignment).
2) Route 25% of traffic to Redwood Hosted fallback pool in us-west2 (no model change) — reduces queue pressure; requires permission from the customer.
3) Apply client-rate soft-throttles and reduce default max_tokens on heavy endpoints to cut per-request compute for the next 30 minutes.

If we don't act quickly we will continue to see 5xx spikes until the autoscaler completes manual remediation (which is estimated 35–50 minutes given current placement constraints).

I'll prepare an incident ticket and a short post-incident note to share.

—Evelyn
SRE Lead, Serving Runtime

John — thank you for the patience. Quick update and next steps: 

What we found: autoscaler placement failures for your Dedicated pool created a brief period of GPU capacity exhaustion; repeated client retries amplified queue length and produced 429s/5xx while the scaler attempted allocation.

What we're doing now (effective immediately):
- We've provisionally added +4 GPUs to your Dedicated pool and are monitoring the allocator (60-minute temporary boost).
- We're requesting permission to route up to 25% of traffic to our Hosted fallback pool in us-west2 while your Dedicated pool stabilizes. This will not change model behavior or outputs.
- We've asked your SREs to hold retries for 60s and to reduce max_tokens on the heaviest endpoints; that will limit per-request compute and reduce queue pressure.

ETA: we expect error rates to materially improve within 15–25 minutes after the boost and failover are in place. We'll keep you updated every 15 minutes and follow up with a full incident summary and recommended quota/placement changes to avoid recurrence.

Please reply with a quick "approve" if you're OK with the 25% hosted fallback route. If you prefer us to avoid routing, we will continue manual remediation but ETA will be longer.

Apologies for the disruption — we're treating this as a high-priority incident.

Thanks,
Logan Wright
